# $crav1-finalize-commit

lane: cross-cutting | group: Commit and pull request | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Draft the commit message, then commit, copy, change, or stop.
use_when: You want the commit message, or the commit itself
reads: Only write the message: Reads the staged or unstaged diff, recent `git log`, an existing persist rule, and `work-item.md` when it exists. The mention picks the id whose milestone or slice label matches the slice being worked, asks when that is unclear, and still reads a single unlabeled line. Commit: Reads the same commit inputs through draft.
writes: Only write the message: Writes a host persist rule only when the user chooses onward. Commit: Writes the persist rule when onward is chosen, and the git commit when the user picks commit. When behind, a merge commit from the pull path, with kit-file conflicts resolved and note indexes rebuilt. A stamp-only `walk-progress.md` conflict is settled into that merge.
leaves alone: Only write the message: Leaves the git commit alone. Commit: Leaves push alone.
limits: Only write the message: commits only when the user also asked to commit in that turn. Commit: the worker commits immediately and skips the menu.
flow:
- `scripts/ending.py --vendor codex` prints the ending from the shared run-ending helper, Run next first.
- Before a write, the same helper's stay card applies when a `design/<topic>` branch is checked out or owns the change, and the card never offers a switch to the default branch.
- a task recorded merged on the host but not ticked is not a reason to recommend `stop`.
- `scripts/task_state.py commit-check --root <spec-folder>` (a thin wrapper over the shared crav1-tasks-ready-to-build module) lists it as tick pending, recommends `commit`, and gives the Run next entry: the verify step, or the tick once verify passes it.
- every ending, `commit`, `copy`, `stop` or a failed commit, is Run next or nothing, never a `Next:` line; a suggestion to throw an edit away is a plain sentence with the git command in a code span.
- A typed `commit` or `commit-now` still asks, with `stop` recommended, when the only changed files are kit-rewritten files (`build-map.md`, `walk-progress.md`, `build-progress/*`) whose values disagree with `verify.md` or `build-progress`, such as a done hash.
- every case ends with Run next, never a `Next:` line: `Push the specs repo:` with `git push`, `Push and open the pull request:` with `$crav1-open-pr`, or `Push to PR <n> and comment:` with `$crav1-open-pr pr<n>`.
- the commit steps are read only after `commit` or `commit-now`.
- a merge of `spec.md` keeps every `Approved:` line under `## Approval needed`.
- The pull path never drops one.
- never commits implementation code on a base branch, even with `commit-now`; the prompt becomes `Commit on a work branch?` (create `feat/<slug>` from the into branch and commit, an existing branch, another name, stop).
- a typed branch name on that prompt is the card's free-text answer, hint `Type a branch name`.
- **`$crav1-finalize-commit`** always drafts first, then offers commit, copy, change, or stop (1.83.0; there is no opening question).
- When no style rule is saved, it drafts in the recommended style and asks CRAV1 style or git log in the same prompt as those choices, at most once per run.
- `message-only` drafts with no commit, the same as copy, and a headless run with no choice word ends as copy.
- Only write the message (was `$crav1-draft-commit-message`): Paste-ready Summary/Description for any git client; CRAV1 style or live git log, once or onward (deletable rule); does not commit unless they ask.
- Optional Azure Boards mention from `docs/specs/<slug>/work-item.md` is the last description line.
- A build-progress conflict that is only hash lines is settled on the pull path, the same way as walk-progress.md.
- when an unfinished build walk is on this branch, the ending is a Run next entry with the command that resumes it, `$crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>` for a whole-branch run, otherwise `$crav1-build-walk <slug> T#`, not a bare `Next: $crav1-build-walk` line.
- Commit (was `$crav1-finalize-commit`): Same draft, then **commit first**, then copy for your git client, change (edit or rewrite), or stop (no push).
- Keeps that mention through the HEAD check and the strip of the known tool trailers it did not write (the list in `references/tool-trailers.md`: Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Aider, Codex, Gemini, Jules, Devin and more); `Signed-off-by` and a real person's `Co-authored-by` stay.
- Trailer hook: asked once per repo in the same prompt, "Strip tool trailers on every commit for this repo?".
- `strip-trailers` writes a committed `.githooks/commit-msg` (POSIX sh) that removes only the known tool trailers in `references/tool-trailers.md`, runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, and saves the answer in a `trailer-hook` rule.
- `Signed-off-by` and human `Co-authored-by` lines stay.
- `keep-trailers` saves no and never asks again.
- Fetch, pull and check (1.81.0, 1.123.0): after the commit it fetches.
- When the branch is behind its upstream it merges with `git pull --no-rebase --no-commit` (never a rebase, never an automatic merge commit) and resolves conflicts in specs, system files and notes by the kit's rules: both sides' added lines kept, ours first; the newest `Synced at` entry per branch; note indexes rebuilt with `notes_index.py` and folded into the one merge commit, noted in that message.
- `scripts/nothing_lost.py` is the check; say nothing was lost only when it reports that.
- One question only when the two sides say different things about the same fact: keep both (a `**Conflict:**` line), mine, theirs, or stop.
- `pull` does this with no commit first.
- It never pushes.
- Next follows run-ending.md: an unfinished walk resumes the walk; a base branch says to push; a feature branch names `$crav1-open-pr`.
- a conflict in `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md` whose every hunk is only a version line (`Spec version`, `Plan version`, `Tasks version`, `Verify version`, `Spec body`, `Questions version`, `Kept questions`, `Section stamps`, `Question ids`, `Content stamp`, `Key`, or `Playbook:`) is settled by `walk_progress.py resolve-stamps --root <spec-folder> --yes --vendor codex`.
- It rewrites a hash to the merged file's normalized hash only when at least one side's recorded hash matches that side's file and every matching side differs from the merge only by progress (line endings, and for spec and tasks a checkbox or a `(PR n)` or `(done)` mark).
- `Done` and `Result` stay.
- A hunk that touches `Done`, `Result`, or any other recorded line is not rewritten.
- The run shows which hunks are stamp-only and offers `settle stamps`.
- a teammate with `.githooks/commit-msg` but no `core.hooksPath` is asked `turn-on-hook` / `skip-hook` in the same choices prompt; the config is never set silently, and the `strip-trailers` option names the `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` line it runs.

## Choice words
- question: Commit or message
  - `commit`: the same as commit now
  - `message-only`: draft and show, no git commit; the same as copy
  - `commit-now`: draft, show, then commit with no choice question (never pushes)
- question: Base branch
  - `new-branch`: code staged on a base branch: create feat/<slug> from the into branch and commit there
- question: Pull
  - `pull`: fetch, then the pull path or the nothing-lost check, with no commit first
- question: Style
  - `crav1`: CRAV1 style, this commit only
  - `git-log`: match git log, this commit only
- question: Trailer hook
  - `strip-trailers`: add the shared .githooks/commit-msg hook that strips known tool trailers, and save yes; on commit, the hook and its project rule go into that commit
  - `keep-trailers`: no hook; save no so it is not asked again
called_by: Called by the user and by `$crav1-finalize-commit`.
runs by itself: Only write the message: Calls no skill. Commit: Calls `$crav1-finalize-commit`.
you run next: $crav1-open-pr
first: `$crav1-finalize-commit`
